newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate 70 bsp higher at 12.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate 70 bsp higher at 12.7 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average lending rate added 70 basis points to 12.7 percent on Thursday as lenders kept short-term interest rates higher after raising them earlier in the week.
Daily settlements totalled 19.9 million kuna against supply at 40 million, and demand at 25 million could not be met entirely, dealers said.
Fresh borrowings accounted for only 8.0 million kuna most of which was call money granted at a steady 11 percent, with the rest sold in 14- and 30-day deals at 13-16 percent.
Insurers rolled over 4.0 million kuna of old loans at an unchanged 9.0 percent, while rates for interbank term loans ranged between 13 and 17 percent.

National Bank of Croatia calculated its kuna midrates for Friday firmer at 5.9922 against the dollar and slightly changed at 3.57530 versus the German mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
